note: Hand-written Grade 4 Core-word content, layered over the draft so it always wins. A word appears here when the course had nothing for it, or had it at the wrong reading level, or - most often in this grade - in a sense from another unit entirely. Cast is Grade 4's own: Amal, Nora, Leo, Sami, Maya, Noah, Elena, Adam, Idris, Hana, Theo, Talia, Teacher Yasmin. Sentences are capped at 80 characters and 16 words, which is what Grade 4's own authored sets already ask a reader to handle.

absorb.childMeaning: To take in or soak up a liquid or gas.
practiceSentences: Dry soil will absorb the rain very quickly.
Which cloth can absorb the most water?
Plants absorb water through their roots.
Dark surfaces absorb more heat than pale ones.
The sponge absorbed the whole spill.

account.childMeaning: A record that lets you sign in to a website with your own name.
account.repitchedFrom: grade 8, which carried two senses at once - the online profile AND 'a description of what happened'. One card teaches one sense.
practiceSentences: Amal opened an account on the reading website.
Do you need an account to watch the video?
Keep your account details private at all times.
The library account lets Leo reserve books.
Nora forgot the password for her account.

application.childMeaning: A program you open on a phone or computer to do a job.
application.repitchedFrom: grade 8: 'A practical use to which something, especially knowledge, is put' - the ABSTRACT sense. This unit is about devices, where an application is an app.
practiceSentences: This application helps you learn new words.
Which application do you use for drawing?
The weather application shows rain tomorrow.
Sami downloaded a maths application last week.
An application must be updated from time to time.

approximate.childMeaning: Close to the real amount, but not exact.
practiceSentences: Give me an approximate depth of the lake.
Is that an approximate or an exact figure?
The approximate temperature was twenty degrees.
An approximate answer is enough for this task.
Sami wrote the approximate weight in his notes.

atmosphere.childMeaning: The layer of gases that surrounds the Earth.
atmosphere.repitchedFrom: grade 7: 'the general mood or feeling that surrounds a place or event' - the MOOD sense, in a Nature & Weather unit. This is the clearest wrong-sense case in the grade so far.
practiceSentences: The atmosphere protects us from the sun's rays.
How thick is the Earth's atmosphere?
Smoke from fires pollutes the atmosphere.
Clouds form in the lower part of the atmosphere.
Gases in the atmosphere trap some of the heat.

audio.childMeaning: Sound that has been recorded so you can listen to it.
practiceSentences: The audio was too quiet to hear properly.
Can you turn the audio up a little?
Nora recorded the audio for the class podcast.
This book comes with audio of every chapter.
Poor audio spoils an otherwise good video.

biography.childMeaning: The true story of a real person's life, written by somebody else.
biography.repitchedFrom: grade 7 - the same sense, at 86 characters.
practiceSentences: Nora read a biography of a famous doctor.
Whose biography did you choose for your project?
The biography described his childhood in detail.
A biography is written about someone, not by them.
Maya is writing a short biography of her grandmother.

browser.childMeaning: A program you use to look at pages on the internet.
practiceSentences: Open the browser and type in the address.
Which browser is on the school computers?
The browser saved the page for later reading.
A browser shows you one webpage at a time.
Leo closed the browser when the lesson ended.

button.childMeaning: A small part that you press to make a machine or device work.
practiceSentences: Press the green button to start the machine.
Which button turns the volume down?
Amal pressed the button and the lift moved.
A red button stops the whole conveyor belt.
Do not press that button without asking first.

circuit.childMeaning: A complete path that electricity can flow around.
practiceSentences: The bulb lit when the circuit was complete.
Why did the circuit stop working?
A broken wire leaves a gap in the circuit.
Leo built a simple circuit with a battery.
Every circuit needs a source of power.

code.childMeaning: Instructions written in a special language that tell a computer what to do.
code.repitchedFrom: grade 6: 'A system of letters, numbers or symbols used to hide or send a message' - the SECRET-CODE sense. This unit sits beside robot, software and application, where code is what a program is made of.
practiceSentences: Leo wrote code to make the robot turn left.
Can you fix the mistake in this code?
The code repeats the same step ten times.
Nora learned to write code at the club.
A single wrong letter can break the whole code.

conservation.childMeaning: Looking after nature so it is not damaged or used up.
practiceSentences: Conservation protects the forest and its animals.
What can our class do for conservation?
Water conservation matters in a dry season.
The park has a conservation area for birds.
Nora joined a conservation club after school.

convenient.childMeaning: Easy to use or do, because it saves you time or trouble.
convenient.repitchedFrom: grade 8 - the same sense, but two clauses joined by 'or'.
practiceSentences: The bus stop is convenient for our house.
Would Saturday be a convenient day to meet?
A convenient shortcut cut ten minutes off the walk.
Online shopping is convenient but not always cheaper.
Amal found a convenient place to keep her keys.
The website is currently closed for repairs.
What are you currently reading, Nora?
Sami is currently working on his project.
The network is currently very slow.
We are currently learning about the water cycle.

data.childMeaning: Facts, numbers or measurements collected together.
practiceSentences: The class collected data about favourite fruits.
What does the data tell us about rainfall?
Amal recorded her data in a neat table.
Good data helps you answer a question properly.
The data showed that Monday was the wettest day.

database.childMeaning: A large, organised store of information kept on a computer.
practiceSentences: The library database lists every book they own.
How do you search this database?
A database can hold millions of records.
Sami added his results to the class database.
The database sorted the names into order.

device.childMeaning: A machine or tool made to do a particular job.
practiceSentences: A tablet is a device you can carry easily.
Which device do you use to read at home?
This device measures the temperature of the room.
Leo charged his device before the journey.
Every device in the room needs a password.

digital.childMeaning: Using numbers and electronic signals, as a computer does.
practiceSentences: A digital clock shows the time in numbers.
Do you prefer a digital or a paper diary?
Amal keeps a digital copy of her drawings.
The museum has a digital map of the building.
Digital photographs are easy to share.

dissolve.childMeaning: To mix into a liquid until it cannot be seen.
practiceSentences: Sugar will dissolve quickly in hot tea.
Does salt dissolve faster in warm water?
Stir the powder until the grains dissolve.
Some substances never dissolve at all.
Nora timed how long the tablet took to dissolve.

download.childMeaning: To copy a file from the internet onto your own device.
practiceSentences: Nora will download the story to read later.
How long does the download take?
The file was too large to download quickly.
Always download from a website you trust.
Sami downloaded a map before the walk.

ecosystem.childMeaning: A community of living things and the place they all depend on.
ecosystem.repitchedFrom: grade 6 - the same sense at 81 characters, one over this grade's cap. Its five sentences were Grade 6 too, naming Doctor Alina, who is not in Grade 4's cast, and three ran past the cap.
practiceSentences: A pond is a small ecosystem full of life.
How does one missing animal change an ecosystem?
The forest ecosystem includes plants and insects.
Pollution can damage a whole ecosystem quickly.
Amal drew the ecosystem of the river bank.

efficient.note: Meaning kept. The five sentences were Grade 6 sports-science - a trained heart pumping more blood per beat, warm-ups and training minutes - and four ran past the 80-character cap. The Grade 6 meaning was correct and is adopted here in a tightened form, so it is a decision rather than an inheritance.
practiceSentences: An efficient worker finishes without wasting time.
How can we make our morning routine more efficient?
The new machine is far more efficient than the old one.
Nora found an efficient way to sort the books.
Efficient lights use less electricity.
efficient.childMeaning: Working well without wasting time, energy or effort.

electronic.childMeaning: Worked by tiny electric parts, like a computer or a phone.
practiceSentences: An electronic keyboard needs no strings.
Is that an electronic thermometer?
The shop sells electronic parts for repairs.
Electronic tickets are sent straight to your phone.
Leo built a simple electronic circuit at school.

element.childMeaning: One of the simple substances that everything is made from.
practiceSentences: Oxygen is an element found in the air.
How many element names can you list?
Iron is a common element in the Earth's crust.
Each element has its own short symbol.
Water is not an element but a compound.

engine.note: The Grade 4 machine sense is kept - it is this grade's own, complete, and already recorded. Worth knowing that the supplied list groups `engine` with browser and webpage, so a SEARCH engine may have been intended; that sense is not taught here, because putting two unrelated senses on one card teaches neither.
extraSentences: The engine of the boat coughed and then started.

evaporation.childMeaning: The change of a liquid into a gas as it warms.
practiceSentences: Evaporation turns the puddle into water vapour.
What causes evaporation to happen faster?
Heat from the sun speeds up evaporation.
The class measured evaporation from two dishes.
Evaporation is one step in the water cycle.

extinct.childMeaning: No longer existing anywhere, with none left alive.
practiceSentences: The dodo has been extinct for centuries.
Which animals became extinct most recently?
Hunting made several species extinct.
An extinct volcano will not erupt again.
Leo read about extinct animals at the museum.

friction.childMeaning: The force that slows things down when they rub together.
practiceSentences: Friction between the tyres and road stops the car.
Does friction make the surface feel warm?
Oil reduces friction inside the engine.
Rough ground creates more friction than ice.
Leo rubbed his hands to feel the friction.

geography.childMeaning: The study of the Earth, its countries, and the people who live there.
geography.repitchedFrom: grade 8: 'The physical features of a place, such as its land, rivers, and distance from other places' - the features THEMSELVES rather than the subject a child studies.
practiceSentences: Geography is my favourite subject at school.
What did you learn in geography today?
The geography of the island makes farming hard.
Our geography lesson covered rivers and mountains.
Maps are an important tool in geography.

gravity.childMeaning: The force that pulls everything towards the Earth.
practiceSentences: Gravity pulls the apple down from the tree.
What would happen to us without gravity?
Gravity keeps the moon circling the Earth.
Rain falls because gravity pulls it downwards.
Amal tested gravity by dropping two stones.

greater.childMeaning: Larger or more important than something else.
greater.repitchedFrom: grade 8 - the same sense at 80 characters, listing four dimensions where one would do.
practiceSentences: The greater the heat, the faster water evaporates.
Which lake has the greater depth?
A greater number of birds arrived this spring.
Wind has greater force on the open hillside.
The greater danger came from the rising river.

image.childMeaning: A picture, especially one on a screen or in a book.
image.repitchedFrom: grade 5: 'A picture that forms in your mind, often created through words or art' - the LITERARY imagery sense. Here the word sits beside video, upload and profile, where an image is a file you can see.
practiceSentences: The image on the screen was very clear.
Which image will you use for the poster?
Amal saved the image to her folder.
A blurred image is hard to understand.
The book has one image on every page.

extraSentences: Reply immediately if the message is urgent.

practiceSentences: Football is an international game.
Have you ever taken an international flight?
The school held an international food day.
An international team studied the coral reef.
English is used for international business.

invisible.childMeaning: Not able to be seen at all.
invisible.repitchedFrom: grade 8: 'Impossible to see, either literally or because it goes unnoticed' - the second clause is the figurative sense, which belongs to a literature unit, not a science one.
practiceSentences: Air is invisible but you can feel it move.
What makes the gas invisible to our eyes?
Water vapour is invisible in the atmosphere.
Germs are invisible without a microscope.
The wind is invisible, yet it bends the trees.

layer.childMeaning: One thickness of something lying over or under another.
practiceSentences: A layer of cloud covered the whole valley.
Which layer of soil holds the most water?
Snow left a thin layer on the playground.
The atmosphere has more than one layer.
Nora drew each layer of rock in her notebook.

lesser.childMeaning: Smaller or less important than something else.
practiceSentences: The lesser storm passed without any damage.
Which is the lesser of the two amounts?
A lesser known bird nests along this river.
The lesser slope was easier to climb.
Heat loss was the lesser of our two problems.

likely.repitchedFrom: grade 7: 'Probable, or expected to happen based on what is already known' - defines the word with itself.
practiceSentences: Rain is likely later this afternoon.
Which animal is most likely to survive here?
It is likely that the river will rise.
A cloudy morning makes a wet day likely.
Frost is likely when the sky is clear.

link.childMeaning: A word or picture you tap to open another page online.
link.repitchedFrom: grade 6: 'A single part of a chain that connects to the parts around it' - the CHAIN sense. A Grade 4 reader meeting `link` in a unit about being online needs the one they can tap.
practiceSentences: Tap the blue link to open the article.
Where does this link take you?
Nora sent me a link to the weather page.
A broken link leads to nothing at all.
The link at the bottom opens the whole report.

loudly.childMeaning: In a way that makes a lot of noise.
practiceSentences: Thunder rumbled loudly above the school.
Why is the wind howling so loudly tonight?
The rain drummed loudly on the metal roof.
Amal read her weather report loudly and clearly.
Waves crashed loudly against the rocks.

major.childMeaning: Large or important, especially compared with others.
practiceSentences: Pollution is a major problem for the river.
What was the major cause of the flood?
A major storm damaged the coastal road.
The major rivers all flow towards the sea.
Losing the forest would be a major loss.

maximum.childMeaning: The largest amount that is possible or allowed.
practiceSentences: The maximum temperature today was thirty degrees.
What is the maximum depth of this pool?
The jar holds a maximum of two litres.
Wind reached its maximum speed at midnight.
Amal recorded the maximum rainfall for June.

media.childMeaning: The ways news and stories reach people, such as television and the internet.
media.repitchedFrom: grade 6 - the same sense at 95 characters, which is past this grade's cap.
practiceSentences: The media reported the storm all week.
How do the media choose their main story?
Maya wants to work in the media one day.
Social media lets people share their own news.
The media showed pictures of the flooded road.

memory.childMeaning: The part of a computer or phone that stores information.
memory.repitchedFrom: grade 2: 'the ability to remember things you have learned or seen' - HUMAN memory, and correct in its own unit. Here the word sits with storage, device and database.
practiceSentences: This device has enough memory for many photographs.
How much memory does your tablet have?
The memory was full, so nothing else would save.
A memory card holds thousands of images.
Deleting old files frees up some memory.

minor.childMeaning: Small in size, importance or seriousness.
practiceSentences: The storm caused only minor damage.
Is that a minor or a major difference?
A minor change in temperature can matter.
Leo made a minor error in his measurement.
Minor cracks appeared after the dry spell.

mixture.childMeaning: A combination of two or more different things.
practiceSentences: Sand and salt together make a simple mixture.
How can you separate this mixture?
The mixture turned cloudy when she stirred it.
A mixture can be pulled apart again.
Leo poured the mixture through filter paper.

nearby.childMeaning: Close to where you are, not far away.
practiceSentences: A nearby stream feeds the village well.
Is there a nearby shelter from the rain?
The nearby hills were covered in mist.
Birds nest in the nearby trees each spring.
We measured rainfall at a nearby station.

network.childMeaning: A group of computers or people joined so they can share things.
practiceSentences: The school network connects every classroom.
Is the network working this morning?
A slow network makes videos stop and start.
Leo joined the network with a password.
The network links four buildings together.

obvious.childMeaning: Very easy to see or understand.
practiceSentences: The damage to the roof was obvious.
Was the answer obvious to everyone else?
There was an obvious crack in the rock.
It is obvious that the pond is drying up.
Amal spotted the obvious mistake at once.
Amal is online, so we can send a message.
Are the results online yet?
The shop sells its books online as well.
Stay safe when you are online.
Our lesson moved online during the storm.

opposite.childMeaning: Completely different from something, or on the other side of it.
practiceSentences: Evaporation is the opposite of condensation.
Which word is the opposite of visible?
The wind blew from the opposite direction.
Their results were the opposite of ours.
The shop stands opposite the weather station.

password.childMeaning: A secret word or set of letters that lets only you sign in.
practiceSentences: Never tell anyone your password.
Have you forgotten your password again?
A strong password mixes letters and numbers.
Nora changed her password every month.
The password must be at least eight letters.

platform.childMeaning: A website or app where people share things with each other.
platform.repitchedFrom: grade 6: 'A flat, raised surface or structure that people can stand or build on' - the PHYSICAL sense. This unit means the kind you post on.
practiceSentences: The class uses a platform to hand in homework.
Which platform do you use to share photographs?
This platform lets you write and read reviews.
Every platform has its own rules for users.
Maya posted her article on a news platform.

pressure.childMeaning: A pushing force, such as the weight of air pressing down.
pressure.repitchedFrom: grade 4 unit 5: 'The feeling of being pushed or stressed by something', with sentences about penalty kicks and tests. Correct in ITS unit and wrong in a weather one - and note it came from this grade's own work, not from above.
practiceSentences: Air pressure falls before a storm arrives.
How does pressure change high on a mountain?
The pressure of the water burst the old pipe.
Low pressure often brings rain and wind.
Sami measured the pressure with a barometer.

privacy.childMeaning: Keeping your own information away from other people.
practiceSentences: Privacy means not sharing your address online.
Why is privacy important on the internet?
The website explains its privacy rules clearly.
Amal values her privacy when she is writing.
Good privacy settings protect your photographs.

profile.childMeaning: A page that shows who you are on a website.
practiceSentences: Leo added a photograph to his profile.
Is your profile set to private?
The profile shows only her first name.
Check your profile before you share it.
A school profile lists your class and year.

quickly.childMeaning: In a fast way, taking little time.
practiceSentences: The rain clouds moved quickly across the sky.
How quickly can you finish the diagram?
Amal quickly wrote down the temperature.
Water evaporates quickly on a hot day.
The storm passed more quickly than we expected.
Snow fell quietly through the whole night.
Can you close the door quietly, please?
Nora quietly watched the bird build its nest.
The stream ran quietly under the bridge.
Sami quietly recorded the wind speed each hour.
Amal recently joined the reading club.
Have you recently changed your password?
The school recently bought twenty tablets.
Leo recently learned to write simple code.
We recently moved to a house near the market.

renewable.note: Meaning kept. The Grade 6 sentences ran to 84 characters and carried Grade 6 material - ozone layers, an engineer, a display promising 'renewable hope'. The Grade 6 meaning was correct; it is adopted here in a shorter form, as a decision rather than an inheritance.
practiceSentences: Wind is a renewable source of energy.
Why is renewable power better for the air?
Solar panels use renewable energy from the sun.
Renewable energy will not run out.
Our school hopes to use renewable electricity.
renewable.childMeaning: Able to be replaced naturally, so it never runs out.

resource.childMeaning: Something useful from nature that people can use.
resource.repitchedFrom: grade 8: 'Something useful that can be used to help achieve a goal' - the abstract planning sense. This unit means water, wood and coal.
practiceSentences: Water is our most precious natural resource.
Is coal a resource that will run out?
Wood is a resource we must use carefully.
The country's main resource is its farmland.
Sami listed every resource the forest provides.

robot.childMeaning: A machine that can be programmed to do a job by itself.
practiceSentences: The robot picked up the block and moved it.
Can a robot really tidy a whole room?
Nora built a robot from a kit at the club.
A robot follows the code you write for it.
This robot vacuums the floor every morning.

extraSentences: The phone had no signal inside the long tunnel.

slowly.childMeaning: Not quickly, taking your time to do something.
practiceSentences: The glacier moves slowly down the valley.
Why does the puddle dry so slowly today?
Leo slowly poured the water into the jar.
Heavy clouds drifted slowly over the hill.
Read the instructions slowly and carefully.

software.childMeaning: The programs that tell a computer what to do.
practiceSentences: New software makes the tablet run faster.
Which software do you use to edit pictures?
The software needs updating every few months.
Sami learned drawing software in one afternoon.
Software is the part you cannot touch.

storage.childMeaning: Space where things or files are kept until they are needed.
practiceSentences: The cupboard gives us extra storage for books.
Is there enough storage on your device?
Cloud storage keeps your files on the internet.
Amal moved old photographs into storage.
The school has storage for every class's equipment.

substance.childMeaning: A material that something is made of.
practiceSentences: Salt is a substance that dissolves in water.
Which substance melts at the lowest temperature?
The sticky substance on the leaf was sap.
Every substance has its own weight and feel.
Amal tested each substance with warm water.
The sky suddenly darkened before the storm.
Did the wind suddenly change direction?
Rain suddenly began during the football match.
The temperature dropped suddenly after sunset.
Leo suddenly noticed frost on the window.

supermarket.childMeaning: A large shop that sells food and many other everyday things.
practiceSentences: Mum bought rice and oil at the supermarket.
Is the supermarket open on Sunday?
The new supermarket has twelve checkouts.
Amal pushed the trolley round the supermarket.
A supermarket sells far more than a small shop.

telephone.childMeaning: A machine that lets you speak to somebody far away.
practiceSentences: The telephone rang just as we sat down to eat.
Who answered the telephone this morning?
Amal used the telephone to call her grandmother.
A telephone line runs along the edge of the road.
Before the telephone, people sent letters instead.

transparent.childMeaning: Clear enough to see straight through.
practiceSentences: The water was transparent right to the bottom.
Is that transparent lid made of glass?
Ice can be transparent or cloudy white.
A transparent bag lets you see what is inside.
Amal used a transparent jar for the experiment.

transport.childMeaning: Ways of carrying people or goods from one place to another.
practiceSentences: Buses are the cheapest transport in our town.
Which transport do you use to reach school?
Public transport was busy on Friday morning.
The city needs better transport for everyone.
Lorries transport food to the market each day.

typical.childMeaning: Showing what something is usually like.
practiceSentences: A typical day in June is hot and dry.
What is typical weather for this season?
Heavy rain is typical of the wet months.
The typical rainfall here is quite low.
Nora described a typical desert plant.
Worms live underneath the top layer of soil.
What is hiding underneath that rock?
The cat sheltered underneath the bench.
Cool air settles underneath the warm air.
Nora found frost underneath the fallen leaves.

upload.childMeaning: To send a file from your device onto the internet.
practiceSentences: Please upload your project before Friday.
How long will the upload take?
Nora will upload the photographs tonight.
A slow connection makes an upload take ages.
Leo uploaded his story to the class page.

username.childMeaning: The name you choose to sign in with on a website.
practiceSentences: Type your username and then your password.
What username did you choose?
Her username is short and easy to remember.
A username should never be your full address.
Sami forgot the username for the reading site.

vibration.childMeaning: A fast shaking movement, often making a sound.
practiceSentences: The vibration of the drum made the sand jump.
Can you feel the vibration through the floor?
Thunder sends a vibration through the air.
A guitar string makes a vibration you can see.
The vibration stopped when the engine cut out.

video.childMeaning: A recording of moving pictures and sound.
practiceSentences: We watched a video about the water cycle.
Did you record a video of the concert?
The video lasted only three minutes.
Amal made a short video for her project.
A video can explain a machine better than words.
The mountain was visible after the fog lifted.
Are the stars visible from here tonight?
Only a thin line of light was visible.
Bacteria are not visible without a microscope.
The comet is visible for a few nights only.

waste.childMeaning: Things that are thrown away because nobody wants them.
waste.note: Grade 1 already teaches the VERB - to use something carelessly. This unit groups the word with conservation and recycling, so it takes the noun, and the two grades teach different parts of speech rather than the same one twice.
practiceSentences: The class sorted the waste for recycling.
Where does all our waste actually go?
Plastic waste harms fish in the ocean.
Food waste can be turned into compost.
Reducing waste is easier than cleaning it up.

webpage.childMeaning: One page on the internet that you can read on a screen.
practiceSentences: This webpage explains how volcanoes form.
Who wrote the webpage about our school?
The webpage took a long time to load.
Amal printed the webpage for her folder.
Every webpage has its own address.
